designRule: This draft contains null candidate-input digests by design. Future lock.json binds final spec.json, protocol.json, adversarial/core_manifest.json and Constitution bytes without any input file referring to its own digest. Filling the nulls now would fabricate a lock (Article 40).
canonicalisationRules: LF line endings only; no CR byte anywhere in the file
file ends with exactly one LF
serialised as json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) followed by a single newline

actual bytes must equal (json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + '
').encode('utf-8')
the digest is taken over those final bytes on disk, so anyone can verify with sha256sum
enforced in-repo by the current explicit .gitattributes entries
canonicalisationNote: RFC 8785 (JCS) was considered and not adopted: exact-bytes hashing is verifiable with standard tools and is easier to audit. Switching to JCS later would be a protocol version change, not an in-place edit.

lockSha256Definition.input: UTF-8 bytes of the seven content fields, in the registered order, each followed by a single newline
lockSha256Definition.formula: lockSha256 = SHA256(specSha256 + LF + protocolSha256 + LF + adversarialManifestSha256 + LF + constitutionSha256 + LF + constitutionVersion + LF + lockVersion + LF + lockedAt + LF)
lockSha256Definition.selfReferenceNote: lockSha256 is excluded from its own input, so this is a checksum over the other fields rather than a self-referential hash.

preconditions: PRELOCK_VALIDATION passes without requiring a final lock.json
spec.json, protocol.json and adversarial/core_manifest.json each equal the one canonical JSON serializer output
none of the three hash inputs contains a self digest
spec, protocol, lock draft and adversarial manifest schemas and semantic constraints pass
the antiCollision check in protocol.json passes
all core-suite expected verdicts exist in adversarial/core_manifest.json before the suite is first executed
human approval to enter P2 has been recorded

verification.statement: Re-runnable by anyone, at any time, with no state from the locking session.
steps: sha256(lockSha256Definition.input rebuilt from this file) == lockSha256

postLockRule: Any change to spec.json, protocol.json or adversarial/core_manifest.json requires a new versioned artifact set and new lock.json. In-place editing followed by recomputing the hash is forbidden (Articles 2 and 59). Adversarial case B8 exercises this path.
integrityNote: lock.json's own file bytes are not hashed by anything. Its integrity comes from git history plus lockSha256 over its content fields. Making it hash itself would reintroduce exactly the self-reference this structure exists to remove.
